newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania Savings in conversion plan.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania Savings in conversion plan.

text.p: Pennsylvania Savings Bank said Friday it had entered into an agreement with PSB Mutual Holding Co to dissolve the mutual fund and form a new holding company.
The bank said in a statement the boards of directors of both entities each had adopted a conversion plan from mutual holding to stock holding.
It said the mutual fund owned 51 percent of the bank, while depositors held about 46 percent.
The bank said the plan will convert the mutual fund into stock form and create a holding company that will offer stock to the bank's depositors as of June 30, 1996.
Shareholders will exchange their share in the bank for stock in the new holding company at an exchange rate that will maintain their current percentage ownership, it added.
"The amount of stock that will be sold and the exchange ratio will be determined based upon an independent appraisal of Pennsylvania Savings Bank that has not yet been performed," it said.
The bank said Jerome Davis, who owns 9.3 percent of the bank, had agreed not to purchase additional stock and vote in favor of the plan.

"Execution of the agreement and the contemporaneous adoption of the Plan satisfies the objectives of all parties and has resulted in a settlement of the previously reported differences between Mr. Davis and the Bank," it said.
The bank's stock was trading 1/4 higher at 14-3/4 early Friday.
